report_draft:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view (PA). Study date not verified.
CLINICAL INDICATION: Routine surveillance. History of treated breast cancer. No new symptoms.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Not provided in findings.
COMPARISON: Prior chest radiograph, PA. Study date not verified.
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Difference from prior: the current image has slightly higher contrast and penetration, and the breast shadows and left chest wall soft tissues lie differently. This limits confident calls of true change in fine right lower zone markings and subtle lower zone density under the breast shadows.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None marked time-sensitive. Listed first for review, in order: F6 right hilar and infrahilar fullness (indeterminate; the two reads disagreed), then F2 right lower zone linear markings (indeterminate).

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central with slight rightward deviation at the aortic arch, within normal. Carina and main bronchi not narrowed. Lungs well inflated. No consolidation, mass or band-like collapse. Coarse linear markings in the right medial lower zone are more conspicuous than on the prior (F2, indeterminate; both reads indeterminate, technique may explain the difference). A tiny dense focus projects over the right lower zone on the current; see CAN'T DETERMINE. Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides.
- Mediastinum / hila: Aortic knuckle prominent, consistent with an unfolded aorta, similar to prior (F3). Upper mediastinum not widened. Aortopulmonary window not filled in. Right hilar and infrahilar fullness and density, more conspicuous than on the prior, indeterminate (F6). The two blind reads disagreed: one read did not identify it and the other called it indeterminate. Size change is not comparable between the studies. Left hilum not enlarged.
- Pleura: No pleural line to suggest pneumothorax. Right costophrenic angle sharp. Left costophrenic angle appears sharp and is partly overlapped by breast shadow. No visible pleural thickening.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette within normal limits on PA, with clear borders, similar to prior (F4).
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion seen at this resolution. Clavicles and shoulders intact. Mild curvature and degenerative change of the visible spine. Both breast shadows present. No soft tissue gas.
- Devices: Left chest wall implanted device with arcing tubing and a small metallic component over the left mid zone, consistent with an implanted venous access device. Present on both studies, no new device (F1). The central catheter course and tip are not confidently traced.
- Below diaphragm: Both domes well defined, right slightly higher than left. Gastric bubble under the left dome. Several gas-filled bowel loops in the left upper abdomen, more than on the prior, indeterminate (F5). The reads disagreed: only one read identified it, as indeterminate. No free gas under either dome.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Right hilar and infrahilar fullness more conspicuous, indeterminate, reads disagreed (F6). Right lower zone linear markings more conspicuous, indeterminate (F2). Tiny dense right lower zone focus on the current, not clearly seen on the prior (see CAN'T DETERMINE). More left upper abdominal bowel gas, indeterminate, reads disagreed (F5). The device component projects over a higher rib level on the current; true migration cannot be judged because soft tissue and breast position differ.
- Unchanged: Aortic knuckle and upper mediastinal contour (F3). Cardiac silhouette (F4). Implanted venous access device present on both studies, no new device (F1). Left hilum not enlarged on either study.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the tiny dense focus over the right lower zone on the current a true nodule, for example a calcified granuloma, or a vessel end-on? | Reason: The focus is very small, sits among crossing vessels, and is not clearly visible on the prior, which has lower contrast.
